# dsh-pr-gate
> **If this helps you, please give it a star** — it helps others find it. Thanks!

Deterministic write gate for DeepSeek Harness (dsh) —
**the CI gate moved to the moment of the write

erministic write gate for DeepSeek Harness (dsh) —
**the CI gate moved to the moment of the write.**

Every file the agent writes (`write` / `edit` / `str_replace_editor`) passes
the same scope policy a

nd residue rules that
agent-pr-gate applies to PRs
in CI — deny-before-write in `tools/pre-execute`,

residue scan of the written
text in `tools/post-execute`, and a durable content-hashed JSONL ledger

of
every decision. Zero LLM calls in the trust path: the parts of the gate that
must NOT be an LLM

decision. Zero LLM calls in the trust path: the parts of the gate that
must NOT be an LLM live here.
## Why now (checked 2026-10-12)

The review/guard lane in the dsh ecosystem is entirely LLM-shaped:
answer-reviewer plugins re-read t

urns with a second model, `dsh-gungnir`
verifies goal completion from exit codes, and the closest ac

tion-guard
(`cc-safety-net`, 1.6k★ in the Claude ecosystem) blocks destructive commands.
**Nobody ga

tes what the agent writes deterministically** — scope policy,
residue markers, or a durable record t

he CI can consume. That slot is empty,
and this plugin is the agent-pr-gate
engine living inside the
runtime instead of waiting for the PR.
## What it does
| Stage | Hook | Deterministic action |
| Before the write | `tools/pre-execute` | Scope policy: deny globs always win; a non-empty allow li

st means "only these". Denied writes never touch the disk |
| After the write | `tools/post-execute`
| Residue scan of the written text: injection text aimed at reviewers, skipped tests, debug markers

. `warn` (default) logs + ledgers; `block` also fails the write with corrective feedback |
| Always
| JSONL ledger | One line per decision — tool, path, action, `sha256` of content, matched pattern, r
esidue kinds. `agent-pr-gate` CI can consume it as the session-side record |
## One policy, two enforcement points

Point `policyFile` at your repo's `agent-pr-gate.yaml` and the live session
enforces the same allow/

deny the CI gate enforces on PRs — all policy entries
are unioned. Inline `allow`/`deny` config work

enforces on PRs — all policy entries
are unioned. Inline `allow`/`deny` config works without a file.

## Compatibility
- **DSH**: verified against the 0.2.x line (source snapshot 0.2.1-alpha.2); installs on any profile

via `dsh plugin add` (prebuilt `lib/`, no build approval).
- **Node**: >= 20 (CI matrix: Node 20/22/

24 on Ubuntu and Windows).
- **Disposable-profile evidence (2026-10-19)**: `dsh plugin --profile <fr
esh> add github:zhengqiuyang/dsh-pr-gate` → installed in 30s; boot shows `[dsh-pr-gate] active: …`;
`dsh plugin --profile <fresh> remove dsh-pr-gate` → dependencies cleared, bundles restored.
## Develop
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The scope glob semantics and residue rules are vendored from the sibling
`agent-pr-gate` checkout (`
npm run sync`; CI runs `sync --check`).
## Roadmap

- `bash` command write-heuristics (redirect/shell-write detection, warn-only)
- Ledger → GitHub chec

k-run bridge (session attestations surfaced in CI)
- Per-policy selection by agent preset, matching

the CI gate's policy classes
- Claims-vs-diff at turn end (the agent's final summary vs. the session

ate's policy classes
- Claims-vs-diff at turn end (the agent's final summary vs. the session ledger)
## Kill criteria

If dsh ships first-party deterministic write gating, or reviewer plugins
converge on deterministic e

nforcement (they are all LLM-based today), this
freezes at its last working version with a postmorte

m here. The engine stays
owned by agent-pr-gate either way.
## Known limitations
- **Paths are judged by their resolved target** relative to the workspace root — traversal like `src
/../.github/workflows/x.yml` is normalized before matching (fixed in this release). Symlinks are NOT
followed by the pure matcher (documented limitation), and there is an inherent TOCTOU window betwee

n check and write; the host's own permissions remain the hard boundary.
- **Named file tools only.**

`shell` writes, custom tools, and unknown argument shapes are not gated.
- **Residue scan is post-w
rite.** `residueMode: block` fails the tool result but does not roll back a file already on disk; de

fault is `warn`.
- **Empty policy = open.** With no allow/deny entries, every write passes (ledger s
till records `written`).
